correctness.rationale: I reconstructed S4 from permutation products and generated each subgroup by breadth-first search in generator words, then partitioned complete flags into orbits under a single simultaneous conjugation. Exhaustiveness follows by adjoining a generating set one element at a time. The independent counts are 30 subgroups and (28,63,24) proper flags by dimension, with (9,15,6) orbits; no longer flag is possible since four distinct proper subgroup orders in a divisibility chain would end at order at least 16, whereas the last proper order is at most 12. Stabilizers preserve the vertex orders of a flag; two points of a single closed simplex identified in the orbit space have the same supported vertices and coordinates, since at most one vertex of each order is available in that simplex. Thus the closed simplices map injectively to regular CW cells, with the stated face maps. Independently recovered all six listed face-index rows and verified the eight free faces in the frozen certificate after each update. The surviving edges are 1,2,4,6,9,10,13, forming vertex cycle 0–6–2–8–4–1–7–0. This proves the claimed collapse of the actual orbit space, not a poset of individual conjugacy classes, and homotopy equivalence rather than homeomorphism. claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: For S4 let V be the normal Klein four. Every proper subgroup except the four point-stabilizer complements H≅S3 has KV proper: a subgroup of order 12 is A4, and a proper subgroup surjecting onto S4/V≅S3 must otherwise have order 6 and meet V trivially. On deleting the complements, K≤KV≥V gives an equivariant poset contraction. The deleted maximal complements are conjugate and the link of one has two orbits under its self-normalizer H (C2 and C3 sites). In the quotient, collapsing the contractible retained subcomplex gives a cone on two points with the base identified to a point, hence a circle. This independently shows exactly what the complement mechanism can explain; it does not determine the reported orbit counts, face boundaries, or length and sequence of the explicit cellular collapse.

value.rationale: S4 is the first small symmetric-group case in this comparison with genuine two-cell attachments and an orbit loop (S3's quotient gives two isolated points). The exact regular flag-orbit cells and collapse are useful to downstream comparisons of geometric orbit spaces and to distinguish simultaneous flags from vertex conjugacy incidence data. They reproduce and explain what survives and what disappears under explicit elementary moves, rather than merely reporting a homology rank or recomputing the usual subgroup counts. No general family classification or importance for the bare circle equivalence alone is required.
